title: Iran Offers Two-Day Plan to Reopen Hormuz as Doha Talks End Without Breakthrough
dek: Tehran says the U.S. now has the next move after talks with Qatari mediators ended with altered proposals but no deal, while Netanyahu presses for strikes after Tuesday's midterms.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Skyline of Tehran, Iran, seen from Book Garden at sunset with clouds over the city

keyPoints: Iran said Monday it had a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks with the U.S., shortening a process it had earlier put at seven days, AP reported.

Iran's plan would require ships to follow a route agreed with Oman and travel under Iranian supervision. Tehran also wants the U.S. to lift its blockade of Iranian ports and oil sanctions, and to agree to a ceasefire that includes Lebanon, AP reported.

Iranian negotiators left Doha talks with Qatari mediators on Sunday. An official briefed on the talks told Reuters the departure was not due to difficulties, and a draft U.S.-Iran proposal is being circulated.
Axios reported that Netanyahu pressed Trump in a Saturday call to strike Iran soon after Tuesday's midterm elections, while Trump wants to let negotiations play out for now.
body:
Iran said on Monday it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days and resume nuclear talks with the United States, if Washington meets Tehran's demands. The Associated Press reported that the plan shortens a process Iran had previously said could take up to seven days.

## Conditions

Iran's earlier plan listed seven conditions, including lifting the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports, the AP reported. Iran's foreign ministry now says ships passing through a reopened strait would follow a route agreed between Iran and Oman and travel under Iranian supervision. Iranian officials have also said Washington must lift sanctions on Iranian oil sales and agree to a ceasefire that covers Lebanon.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told a weekly news conference that the plan remained the basis for indirect talks with Washington through mediators. He said "the ball is now in the US court." The AP noted that Baghaei did not say Tehran had changed its demands or that Washington had accepted the proposal.

## Doha talks

Iranian negotiators left talks with Qatari mediators in Doha on Sunday, and a draft proposal for a U.S.-Iran deal is being circulated, with a follow-up meeting possible, an official briefed on the talks told Reuters on Monday. Iran's foreign ministry said contacts over ending the eight-month war are continuing, and that the talks ended with altered proposals but no breakthrough, Reuters reported.

## Washington and Israel

Axios reported that Trump had a candid phone call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday about the state of U.S. negotiations with Iran and how quickly to return to combat. Axios also reported that Netanyahu is pressing for a strike immediately after Tuesday's midterm elections, while Trump wants negotiations to play out for now. Axios reported that no final decision on new strikes had been made.

## Wider diplomacy

China plans to send a special envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia in early to mid-November, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told reporters, according to AP. The envoy will focus on easing tensions and promoting regional stability.
